;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[September 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A mine explosion killed at least three people and left another injured in [[Nangarhar Province]], [[Afghanistan]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan/3-civilians-killed-1-wounded-nangarhar-ied-blast (TOLOnews)]
*[[Sudanese conflict in South Kordofan and Blue Nile]]
**[[Prime Minister of Sudan|Prime Minister]] [[Abdalla Hamdok]] and [[Abdelaziz al-Hilu]], the leader of the [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North]] (SPLM–N), sign an agreement to transition [[Sudan|the country]] into a [[secular state]]. The agreement comes three days after the signing of a [[peace deal]] between Sudan's transitional government and the [[Sudan Revolutionary Front]], to which the SPLM–N opted out of. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/government-rebels-agree-to-make-sudan-secular-state/1963047 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**Twenty [[Nigerian soldier]]s are killed after [[Boko Haram]] militants attacks two military positions in [[Borno State|Borno]], [[Nigeria]]. [http://saharareporters.com/2020/09/03/boko-haram-terrorists-kill-20-nigerian-soldiers-borno-attacks (Sahara Reports)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Nana (2020)|Hurricane Nana]]
***Tropical Storm Nana strengthens into a [[Hurricane Nana (2020)|hurricane]] as it is expected to make landfall overnight in [[Belize]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/tropical-storm-nana-headed-belize-72773925 (ABC News)]
***[[Hurricane Nana (2020)|Hurricane Nana]] makes landfall and downgrades to a tropical storm. [https://www.winknews.com/2020/09/03/nana-makes-landfall-in-belize-three-areas-to-watch/ (WINK-TV)]
**[[Hurricane Laura]]
***The death toll from [[Hurricane Laura]] in [[Louisiana]] increases to 17. Eight of the deaths were linked to carbon monoxide poisoning. [https://www.brproud.com/news/hurricane-laura-death-toll-rises-to-17-in-louisiana/ (brproud.com)] [https://people.com/human-interest/nearly-half-deaths-linked-hurricane-laura-caused-generators-family-4/ (''People'')]
*[[2020 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[Typhoon Maysak (2020)|Typhoon Maysak]], the strongest [[typhoon]] of the season, makes [[landfall]] along the southern coast of the [[Korean Peninsula]], southwest of [[Busan]], [[South Korea]]. [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2020/09/01/Typhoon-Maysak-makes-landfall-in-South-Korea/7721598985484/ (UPI)]
**[[Panama]]nian-flagged cargo ship ''[[Gulf Livestock 1]]'' with 43 crew members and thousands of [[cattle]] onboard is reported missing in the [[East China Sea]]. The [[Japan Coast Guard]] says it has found one person drifting in rough waters in a lifejacket. A distress signal was sent from the ship shortly before disappearing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-54008087 (BBC News)]
*A second fire breaks out on board the oil ship [[MT New Diamond|MT ''New Diamond'']] off the coast of [[Sri Lanka]]. The ship departed a port in [[Ahmadi Governorate]], [[Kuwait]], and was headed to the port of [[Paradeep]] in India. Authorities fear the 2 million barrels of oil could cause an "environmental disaster". Russian ships depart to assist and one out of the 23 crew was missing following the incident. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/world/2020/09/03/Second-fire-breaks-out-on-fuel-tanker-sailing-from-Kuwait-to-Sri-Lanka (Reuters via Al Arabiya)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports a record daily jump of 83,883 cases. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-india-cases-idUSKBN25U0H5 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record daily jump of 3,622 new cases in the last 24 hours. Of those new cases, 1,359 are from [[Jakarta]], which also reports the highest single day increase in new cases. [https://m.detik.com/health/berita-detikhealth/d-5158322/tertinggi-sejak-wabah-merebak-ini-sebaran-3622-kasus-baru-corona-indonesia (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports their first case after a streak of 100 days without new cases. [https://www.bloomberg.com/amp/news/articles/2020-09-03/thailand-reports-first-local-case-after-100-day-virus-free-run (Bloomberg.com)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[Pfizer]] CEO [[Albert Bourla]] says that the vaccine trials for Pfizer might have results by October. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/09/03/pfizer-ceo-confirms-coronavirus-vaccine-trial-may-have-results-in-october.html (CNBC)]
***[[GlaxoSmithKline]] and [[Sanofi]] announces that they will start vaccine trials. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-54009633 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The [[United States Department of Defense]] says that the [[United States Armed Forces|United States military]] will choose five treatment facilities to carry advanced testing phases for [[AstraZeneca]] and other vaccine trials. [https://www.urdupoint.com/en/world/us-military-selects-5-new-sites-for-next-phas-1019875.html (UrduPoint)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***The number of cases in [[Brazil]] passes 4 million. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-brazil-idUSKBN25U35Y (Reuters)]
*[[2020 wildfire season]], [[Climate change in the Arctic]]
**The [[Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service]] reports that the [[Arctic Circle]] has experienced its worst [[wildfire]] season on record after the service released data indicating that a series of wildfires occurring in the first half of 2020, mostly in the [[Republics of Russia|Russian republic]] of [[Sakha Republic|Sakha]], have [[Carbon footprint|emitted]] more than 244 million tons of [[carbon dioxide]]. The emissions within that period have increased by more than a third of carbon emissions in the whole of 2019. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-09-03/climate-change-arctic-fires-in-2020-released-record-carbon (Bloomberg)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/09/03/world/arctic-wildfires-climate-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Public Health England]] reports that [[England|the country]] last year had the most cases of [[gonorrhea]] since records began more than 100 years ago, at 70,936 reported cases. Those aged 20–25 had the largest increase, at 28% between 2018 and 2019. [https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-54011133 (BBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Bahrain–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**[[Bahrain]]'s [[Civil Aviation Affairs]] grants [[Freedoms of the air#First freedom|first freedom]] rights to the [[United Arab Emirates]] (UAE), allowing flights between the UAE and any country to enter Bahraini [[airspace]]. Bahrain follows [[Saudi Arabia]] in granting such rights to the UAE, which the latter did two days prior following [[Israel–United Arab Emirates peace agreement|the establishment of diplomatic ties]] between [[Israel]] and the UAE. Like Saudi Arabia and most [[Arab states]], Bahrain currently does not maintain [[Bahrain–Israel relations|any official relations]] with Israel nor [[International recognition of Israel|recognises it]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1729191/middle-east (''Arab News'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-emirates-bahrain-flights/new-bahrain-policy-to-allow-flights-between-israel-and-uae-to-cross-its-airspace-idUSKBN25U304 (Reuters)]
*[[United Nations Secretary General]] [[António Guterres]] urges [[Japan]] and other wealthy nations to give up on their reliance on [[fossil fuel]]s and invest in [[green energy]]. Guterres noted that many countries are using green energy to keep [[global warming]] at {{convert|1.5|C-change|F-change}}. [https://apnews.com/eae7ce5ff108058400f9f0d24466b752 (AP)]

;Law and crime
*[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
**Protesters and [[riot police]] clash in the city of [[Lalitpur, Nepal|Lalitpur]] over the ban of outdoors public events amid a [[religion in Nepal|religious]] festival. The [[government of Nepal|government]] had previously banned public gatherings as the country records a total of 42,877 cases. [https://apnews.com/3d726d195ea49d734ed857a17288aea3 (AP)]
*[[Murder of Ján Kuciak]]
**A [[Bratislava]] court [[Acquittal|acquits]] [[Slovaks|Slovak]] businessman [[Marián Kočner]] for ordering the [[murder]] of [[investigative journalist]] Ján Kuciak and his fiancée Martina Kušnírová in February 2018. The court rules the lack of evidence to convict Kočner. [https://www.dw.com/en/jan-kuciak-murder-slovak-court-finds-businessman-innocent/a-54798653 (DW)]
*[[Vitoria massacre]]
**Former [[Deputy Prime Minister of Spain]] [[Rodolfo Martín Villa]] declares before the [[Argentina|Argentine]] courts accused of [[genocide]] and [[crimes against humanity]] for the role of the police during his tenure as [[Ministry of the Interior (Spain)|Minister of the Interior]] between 1976 and 1979, especially for the Vitoria massacre in 1976. [https://www.20minutos.es/noticia/4369291/0/rodolfo-martin-villa-genocidio-transicion-juicio-argentina/ (20 minutos)]
*[[2020 Solingen killings]]
**Five children who were siblings are found dead in their apartment in [[Solingen]], [[NRW]], [[Germany]]. Their elder brother survived. Their mother, who is injured after throwing herself in front of a train in [[Düsseldorf]], is suspected of the killings. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54012885 (BBC News)]
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]]
**[[Killings of Aaron Danielson and Michael Reinoehl]]
***Michael Reinoehl, who was accused of killing [[Patriot Prayer]] activist Aaron Danielson, is shot dead by police during arrest. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/09/03/us/michael-reinoehl-arrest-portland-shooting.html ('' The New York Times'')]
**[[Killing of Daniel Prude]]
***[[Rochester, New York|Rochester]] police made another round of arrests during protests that at times, turned violent. Protesters gathered and chanted near the Public Safety Building, and tensions began rising around 10:30 p.m. with police deploying pepper spray and pepper balls multiple times in a 10-minute span. [https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nys/rochester/public-safety/2020/09/04/protests-continue-in-rochester-after-daniel-prude-s-death (spectrum local news)]
*A [[Hong Kong]] court acquits [[pro-democracy]] media tycoon [[Jimmy Lai]] of criminal intimidation on a 2017 charge. This verdict comes after his high-profile arrest last month under the new [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|national security law]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-security-jimmylai/hong-kong-court-says-media-tycoon-jimmy-lai-not-guilty-of-criminal-intimidation-in-2017-case-idUSKBN25U167 (Reuters)]
*[[Kuwait]] swears in eight female judges, being the first [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf|Gulf country]] to do so. The women were among 54 judges sworn into the Supreme Court. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/gulf/2020/09/03/Kuwait-swears-in-first-female-judges-in-country-s-history (AFP via AL Arabiya)]
;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Jamaican general election]]
**[[Jamaicans]] head to the polls the elect a new [[parliament of Jamaica|parliament]] amid a surge of [[COVID-19 pandemic in Jamaica|COVID-19 infections]]. [[Prime Minister of Jamaica|Prime Minister]] [[Andrew Holness]] of the [[Jamaica Labour Party|Labour Party]] is among the candidates. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-53997063 (BBC News)] 
**The Jamaica Labour Party wins 49 of 63 seats in a landslide victory, marking the first time that the party has won consecutive general elections since 1967. [https://www.voanews.com/americas/jamaicas-ruling-party-claims-landslide-victory-thursdays-general-election (VOA)]
*[[2020 Bulgarian protests]]
**Protests in [[Bulgaria]] turn violent for the first time, as protesting crowds attempt to storm the nation's [[National Assembly (Bulgaria)|parliament]], leading to a night of fighting between demonstrators and security forces. [https://www.dw.com/en/bulgaria-riots-police-anti-government-protesters-clash-in-sofia/a-54798039 (DW)]

;Science and technology
*The skeletons of 200 [[mammoth]]s, 25 [[camel]]s, and five [[horse]]s are unearthed at a construction site for the [[Mexico City Santa Lucía Airport]]. It surpasses [[Mammoth Site, Hot Springs|Mammoth Site]], [[Hot Springs, South Dakota|Hot Springs]], [[South Dakota]], United States as the largest find of mammoth bones, which had 61 skeletons. [https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/story/2020-09-04/mammoth-central-found-at-mexico-airport-construction-site (''Los Angeles Times'')]
